answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents require every identity to weather a periodic gale of surprise audits: each must re-anchor its reputation by proving unique historical interactions against a live summit of randomized challenges drawn from peer graphs. Genuine agents pass with existing records while a swarm of fakes collapses under simultaneous demand for distinct deep histories. The attacker faces escalating cost because fabricating unique anchors for hundreds of identities during the gale exceeds the value of any single epoch reward, while honest participants pay only routine upkeep.
